title: Barrowlight
intro:
Rain has followed you for three days across the Greywater moor. The villagers of Hollin's Rest would not say the barrow's name. They only pointed north and made the sign of the ash.

Somewhere beneath that mound lies the Barrowlight, the lantern the Ashen Order kept burning so their dead would sleep. It went dark at the turn of the season. Since then, the graves of Hollin's Rest have not stayed shut.

You crest the last hill as dusk bleeds out of the sky, and the lichgate rises before you.

epilogues.text:
Behind you, the Nocturne Beacon chimes across the sunken cathedral, a low amber note that keeps the waking dead lucid without forcing them back into dreamless sleep. Sister Wren stands at the edge of the Lantern Market with her sleeves rolled to the elbow and salt-flakes on her linen, and the Wayfarers have already chalked her name on the pillar beside yours.

The floodgate rises on its groaning winch. Beyond the far arch, black water drains away into the Memory Warrens, where the Hollow Choir keeps its archive of vows and the Ashen garrison scrubs its own soldiers clean of fear. The Barrowlight burns warm and gold in your hand. It has learned, as you have, that a watch can be ended without being betrayed.

You cross the tollbridge with the beacon's chime at your back, {player.name}. For the first time since the lantern died, the dark ahead does not feel like a grave. It feels like a road.

The Nocturne Beacon rings out behind you as you cross the Drowned Tollbridge, its amber light spilling over the black canal. In the Lantern Market the salt-frost is flaking from the spirits' hands, and Keeper Maeve is reading the remembered names aloud from the pillar, one by one, so that none of them slips out of the ink tonight.

No one walks beside you, but you do not leave unwitnessed. The Barrowlight burns gold in your grip, steady as a heartbeat, and the echoes in the wet stone seem to lean toward it as you pass.

Beyond the floodgate the warrens wind deeper, toward older griefs and harder choices. Whatever waits there, {player.name}, Nocturne will remember who relit its bell.

The Nocturne Beacon burns again, but the square went quiet when you carried the tuning-tongue and the lens back through it, still marked by what it cost to take them. The spirits warm their hands at the amber light and do not meet your eyes.

The Barrowlight's flame is thin and ash-pale as you cross the tollbridge. It gives light, and the light is enough to see by, but it no longer leans toward the deep like a compass needle. It simply burns, the way a lamp burns in an empty room.

You mended the light the way the Order would have, {player.name}: with iron, and with a trail of the broken behind you. The warrens ahead will ask whether that was ever the same thing as mercy.

Behind you, the Nocturne Beacon still stands dark. Its bell is silent, and along the colonnade the grey salt-frost keeps creeping across the knuckles of the spirits who waited for it to ring.

Still, the Barrowlight burns gold in your hand. The people you met on the way down, you met as people: a clerk losing his own name, a sister refusing to lose her brother, a soldier who could not keep a promise. The light remembers that, even if the square cannot yet.

The floodgate groans open onto the warrens, {player.name}. You tell yourself you will come back for Nocturne. The black water closes over the causeway behind you, and the dark does not say whether it believes you.

Behind you, Nocturne's beacon is still dark, and the Lantern Market has gone very quiet. The spirits along the colonnade sit with salt crawling up their wrists, and no one calls a name after you as you go.

The Barrowlight burns cold as frost in your grip. In its pale glare the echoes in the stone no longer speak. They only watch.

The floodgate rises on a shriek of rusted iron, and you walk into the warrens alone, {player.name}. The deep has noticed you now. It has not yet decided what you are.

The floodgate grinds open and you cross the Drowned Tollbridge into the dark. The Barrowlight's flame wavers between gold and ash, undecided, much like the Under-Barrow itself.

Behind you, Nocturne's beacon is still dark, and the waking dead of the Lantern Market keep their uneasy watch beneath the broken ribs of the cathedral. Ahead, the Memory Warrens wind down into older griefs.

Whatever you are becoming down here, {player.name}, the next step will decide it.

gameOverText: The cold of the barrow closes over you like deep water. Somewhere far above, rain falls on the lichgate, and the Barrowlight stays dark. Your story ends here, {player.name}.
